rationale: 01-qbsort is a small sorting benchmark (recursive quicksort, bubble sort) dominated by compact, loop/recursion-heavy functions with few calls and few globals, and with an empty static profile the table favors cheap, broadly applicable passes. SUB gets high SecurityGain/DiversityGain with near-zero cost weights since arithmetic substitution is nearly free on this integer-heavy code. FLA gets the strongest security weight because the control flow (sort loops, recursion drivers) is exactly what flattening protects, with moderate cost weights to keep loop-dominated hot functions from excessive slowdown. BCF and SPLIT are enabled at moderate levels: BCF adds meaningful control-flow confusion at acceptable size cost for these tiny functions, while SPLIT is cheap and enlarges the basic-block pool that FLA/BCF transform more effectively. IBR is kept at moderate security/diversity weights with a raised RuntimeCost weight since indirect branching on tight sort-loop back edges is where overhead concentrates. ICALL is only lightly weighted because the benchmark has few call sites to obscure, and IGV is effectively deprioritized (lowest security/diversity weights, highest CorrectnessRisk weight) since the program has minimal global state, so its transformation surface and payoff are both small.
